scope: Theorem 2.2 of the manuscript “The Partition Principle does not imply Choice” (preprints/The-Partition-Principle-does-not-imply-Choice-September-24-2026/partition-principle-without-choice.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 244 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7101fb4828d8d2ba), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 6-7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a monoid T of cardinality µ, with a distinguished e ̸= 1, having the following properties. 1. T is left cancellative and conical, has conditional joins, and has heights and costs satisfying Equation (2.1). 6 2. Every valid finite overlap prescription on copies of T is realized by left translations x 7→ lix in T, with exactly the prescribed identifications. 3. For a, b ∈ T with b ̸= 1, and every ideal U ⊆↓ a, there are µ distinct elements m with mb = ae, m ̸⊑ a, ↓ m∩ ↓ a = U, n ∨ m = ae (n ⊑ a, n / ∈ U). (2.2) The cones of distinct elements in this family intersect exactly in aeT. Moreover |T \eT| = µ. 4. For every countable subset of T there is a countable submonoid T0 containing it and a continuous conservative tower starting at T0 and ending at T. Each successor step has one of the following properties: (a) no new element divides an old element; (b) every new element w with an old right multiple has a least old right multiple g(w), and d old, g(w) ⊑ wd =⇒ wd old. (2.3) Here “old” means belonging to the base of that particular successor step, and the comparisons may be tested in the final monoid.
